hypothesis: Repeated point comparisons rebuild coordinate differences and bounded normal forms. Reuse exact scalar equality and reject certified-separated cached coordinate intervals before constructing those differences.
preservation: True still requires exact coordinate equality; false may remain inconclusive under the existing conservative PartialEq contract.
Use existing exact-rational and structural certificates. A cached interval can prove inequality only when strictly disjoint; touching/overlap must fall back.
Do not initiate numeric refinement or persist a new cache. Aborted or unavailable scalar cache entries fall back.
No Point2/Real layout, public API, policy, tolerance, projection or normalization-budget change.
The cached_rational_interval dependency is itself part of the provisional native-source work; this does not admit it independently.
oracle: Injective exact affine transforms of independent integer point pairs: arbitrary common origins, positive/negative/extreme rational scales, repeated and cloned queries before/after preparation. Supplement with tiny rational separations, unresolved trigonometric zero, abort state and concurrent shared points.
early_validation: Format, focused point unit tests and exact CurvePoint public consumers, strict all-target release curve Clippy, then a matched public equality timing/allocation probe using the preserved baseline. Original curve/native matrix and unchanged full-board gate follow only if correctness and cost support continuing.
retention: Pending: isolated production admission must include the scalar cache API dependency and complete row/report comparison. Neither the contract nor a probe admits the wider native-source candidate.
